# Weaknesses and Future Work

## Weaknesses

Several limitations qualify the interpretation of the present findings.
Most fundamentally, no ground-truth measure of emotional state was
collected against which the derived labels could be validated. Valence
and arousal rest on two independent proxy measures, facial expression
via HSEmotion and HRV via RMSSD, rather than on validated psychological
assessments, and because these channels are processed separately and
combined only afterwards, any inaccuracy specific to either propagates
directly into the resulting label without cross-validation between them.

A structural confound follows from the fixed stimulus order. Since all
participants viewed the same video in the same sequence, labels and
plant recording share a common temporal profile: the labels track the
stimulus timeline, while the plant signal drifts over the session
through electrode settling and changing contact impedance. A model can
therefore exploit position within the session in the absence of any
plant--emotion relationship. Grouping by participant does not remove
this, since the temporal structure is shared across groups rather than
nested within them, and session normalization removes level but not the
shape of the drift.

Construct validity is a related concern. HSEmotion reports categorical
accuracies of roughly 55--70% on standard benchmarks [@savchenko2022];
since these refer to discrete categories, confusions within the same
valence sign do not propagate into the valence label, so the effective
valence error is lower than the categorical figure suggests, though it
was not quantified here. The arousal axis rests on a single HRV measure
whose validity at lower arousal levels has been questioned [@choi2017],
which may have contributed to the weak arousal result, although a
genuinely weak underlying effect is equally consistent with the data.
Discretizing both axes adds further researcher degrees of freedom: the
thresholds and the rule collapsing them into the five-class label were
fixed a priori and not varied.

The stimulus constitutes a further limitation. The video used to elicit
emotional responses was reused from an earlier, unrelated COIN seminar
project [@schafer2025] rather than being normed on valence and arousal
in the manner of standardized stimulus sets such as IAPS. Its capacity
to reliably elicit the intended range of affective states across a
heterogeneous sample was therefore not independently confirmed.

The sample comprises 15 participants and 284 analyzable windows. Since
windows are autocorrelated and nested within participants, the effective
sample size is closer to the number of participants than of windows, and
interval estimates derived at the window level would understate the true
uncertainty. The correlation analysis additionally evaluated 22 features
across two analysis variants without correcting for multiple
comparisons, which should be taken into account when interpreting the
reported significance levels.

As in @gloor2025, a single plant species (*Kalanchoe*) was used
throughout, so generalization across species or specimens remains
untested. *Kalanchoe* is moreover a CAM species whose stomata open
primarily at night, which limits daytime gas exchange and restricts the
CO~2~ control analysis in particular, since daytime plant--CO~2~
coupling would be expected to be stronger in C~3~ species. Unlike
@gloor2025, no sham or shielding controls were included.

The measurement chain imposes its own constraint. The AD8232 is an
analog front end designed for electrocardiography, and its passband is
optimized for cardiac rather than plant biopotentials, whose action and
variation potentials evolve over seconds to minutes. The recorded signal
is therefore band-limited, with slow components attenuated by design,
which qualifies the feature-importance finding below: the weak
contribution of absolute-level features may partly reflect the amplifier
rather than the plant.

Finally, all sessions were conducted on a single day in a room not
isolated from external influences. Room temperature, humidity, and air
movement were neither held constant nor recorded, and their influence on
the plant signal cannot be determined from the present data. Only
ambient CO~2~ was recorded as a mediating channel; participant movement,
which generates air displacement and vibration near the plant, cannot be
excluded as an alternative pathway.

## Future Work

Several directions follow from these findings. The lower accuracy
observed here relative to @gloor2025 is consistent with the more
conservative and generalizable evaluation framework applied, namely
grouped cross-validation across 15 participants and permutation testing.
This interpretation is directly testable: re-evaluating the present data
under a non-grouped, randomly split cross-validation would indicate how
much of the difference is attributable to evaluation protocol rather
than to effect size. Larger and more diverse samples under
professionally controlled laboratory conditions would additionally
narrow the wide confidence intervals observed here and minimize
session-level environmental drift.

The confounds identified above translate directly into design
refinements. Counterbalancing stimulus order across participants
decorrelates the emotion timeline from session time, a time-only
baseline model provides a reference point against which classification
performance can be judged, and block-wise permutation preserves the
autocorrelation structure that free shuffling destroys. Motion energy
extracted from the existing video recordings offers a low-cost control
for movement-mediated coupling.

Operationalizing emotion via the dimensional valence-arousal model
[@russell1980] revealed differential sensitivity across affective
dimensions that a combined categorical label would likely have obscured.
Valence and arousal should therefore be treated as analytically distinct
constructs and modeled as separate targets with dimension-specific
refinements: alternative HRV-based markers beyond RMSSD, given its
documented limitations [@choi2017], and higher-performing FER models
than HSEmotion for valence. Validated self-report instruments such as
the Self-Assessment Manikin [@bradleylang1994] may further strengthen
interpretation, provided they complement rather than replace the
physiological channels employed here.

Environmental variables such as CO~2~ should be recorded explicitly and
controlled statistically, an issue that has received little attention in
research on plant bioelectrical signals; the present analysis indicates
that CO~2~ does not confound the plant-valence relationship. Future
studies could extend this by including volatile organic compound (VOC)
measurements alongside CO~2~ to assess whether other airborne chemical
signals mediate or confound the plant-emotion relationship in ways that
CO~2~ alone cannot capture.

The finding that level-invariant and session-relative features
consistently outranked absolute-level ones contributes to feature
engineering in this domain and helps explain why session-normalized
features tend to yield better performance. The descriptors in question
are Hjorth mobility and complexity, dimensionless ratios and therefore
scale-invariant, unlike Hjorth activity, a variance measure sharing the
level dependence of the amplitude descriptors. Whether the pattern is
physiological or instrumental can only be resolved with instrumentation
matched to the timescale of plant bioelectrical activity: a DC-coupled
electrometer amplifier with high input impedance, non-polarizable
electrodes, and shielded leads would preserve the slow components
attenuated by the ECG front end used here.
